title: FAST-7A: Backlog Depletion RCA and Risk Register Refresh

sourcePlanning.title: Plan backlog replenishment after major backlog depletion alert

events.summary: Backlog depletion alert fired when queue depth reached 0 for trigger fingerprint backlog-under-threshold-restore-10.
Open FAST tasks checked (0) and recent planning runs checked (0).
Planning trigger artifact created for backlog restoration workflow.

incidentSummary.whatHappened: Queue depth depleted to zero before replenishment actions started, forcing reactive planning artifact creation.
incidentSummary.whyItMattered: Zero runnable depth blocked steady campaign execution and increased dependence on manual intervention.

rankedRecurrenceRisks.name: Replenishment trigger latency or automation gap
rankedRecurrenceRisks.validationPlan: Replay trigger events and verify auto-replenishment starts within agreed trigger-to-refill SLA.

rankedRecurrenceRisks.name: Observability blind spot on queue-depth trend and lead indicators
rankedRecurrenceRisks.validationPlan: Run synthetic depletion test and confirm pre-zero warning plus complete timeline event capture.

rankedRecurrenceRisks.name: Single-path recovery dependency on manual planning run
rankedRecurrenceRisks.validationPlan: Execute failover simulation proving a backup path can create an actionable replenishment plan without manual bottleneck.

mitigationRequirements.behavior: When queue depth crosses the configured depletion threshold, the system must initiate replenishment automatically and emit an immutable start marker.
mitigationRequirements.constraints: Must be idempotent per incident correlation key; must not require manual operator action for initial replenishment start; must preserve existing queue safety guardrails.
mitigationRequirements.outcomes: Trigger-to-replenishment start meets agreed SLA for validated replay scenarios.
mitigationRequirements.rollbackExpectations: Rollback mitigation if replenishment-start error rate or start latency exceeds baseline guardrails for two consecutive validation windows.
mitigationRequirements.degradationExpectations: Under rollback or partial outage, switch to safe minimum queue refill behavior and present explicit degraded-mode operator status.

mitigationRequirements.behavior: The incident artifact pipeline must record queue-depth snapshots and lead-indicator signals across the depletion window with ordered timestamps.
mitigationRequirements.constraints: If telemetry is missing or delayed, artifact publication must remain partial until assumptions and validation owner are explicitly recorded.
mitigationRequirements.outcomes: Each incident includes an auditable, end-to-end timeline that supports RCA confidence scoring and replay validation.

mitigationRequirements.behavior: Recovery flow must provide a backup planning path that can produce an actionable replenishment plan when the primary manual path is unavailable.
mitigationRequirements.constraints: Backup path must preserve trigger fingerprint/artifact audit links and must not bypass dedupe checks.
mitigationRequirements.outcomes: Failover simulation confirms planning continuity without single-operator dependency.
mitigationRequirements.rollbackExpectations: Rollback backup path activation if generated plans violate baseline quality or increase restoration latency beyond baseline guardrails.
mitigationRequirements.degradationExpectations: In degraded mode, use the primary path with operator escalation while preserving minimum safe queue refill and status visibility.

dedupeEvidence.notes: Dedupe evidence retained as context input and not treated as direct causal proof.

assumptions: Alert timestamp and planning artifact timestamp are authoritative for the required timeline window.
SLA threshold value is defined externally and enforced during validation execution.
